recognize_zh: 這是右側下肢（膝部與遠端股骨）X 光片翻拍，影像有明顯摩爾紋（moiré），遠端股骨髓腔僅見模糊的斑駁透亮區，病灶邊界與硬化邊緣在此解析度下無法清楚辨識，需搭配另一張影像判讀。
features: Plain radiograph of the right distal femur and knee, photographed from a monitor with moire artifact
Subtle mottled lucency in the distal femoral diaphysis/metaphysis
Well-defined sclerotic margins cannot be confirmed at this resolution
No obvious pathologic fracture, periosteal reaction or soft-tissue mass visible
Image quality limits assessment of lesion number and borders
describe_en: Frontal radiograph of the right distal femur and knee, photographed from a display screen, shows subtle mottled lucency within the distal femoral shaft and metaphysis. Because of moire artifact and low contrast, the size, number and margins of any lytic lesions, including the reported sclerotic rims, cannot be reliably assessed on this image. No obvious pathologic fracture or aggressive periosteal reaction is seen. The image is only partially supportive of the reported lytic lesions and should be interpreted together with better-quality views; in the clinical context, the findings would be compatible with skeletal Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

ddx.vs: Myeloma lesions are punched-out lytic defects without sclerotic rims in adults, often in the axial skeleton.
A Brodie abscess is usually solitary and metaphyseal with a thick sclerotic rim and sometimes a sequestrum.
These produce permeative moth-eaten lysis and metaphyseal lucent bands rather than well-marginated lesions.
Benign fibrous lesions are eccentric cortical, multiloculated or ground-glass lesions, and histology lacks Langerhans cells.
